revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables are each about 7,650 feet long. A supply company sells cable-protection wrap in spools measured in yards. How many yards of protective wrap does one full cable need? Show your work using a conversion factor.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 1 yard = 3 feet, so converting feet to the larger unit (yards) means dividing by the conversion factor: 7,650 ÷ 3 = 2,550 yards. One cable needs 2,550 yards of protective wrap.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do I change one measurement unit into another?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. In this group we go deeper: trickier numbers, a second way to see it, and explaining why it works — not just getting the answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit — and you can explain why it works, even when it gets tricky.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: The cabinet is 5 feet tall. I want to know how many inches that is.
My conversion factor is 1 foot = 12 inches.
Inches are smaller than feet, so I multiply: 5 × 12 = 60.

onLevel.stem: A shelf is 30 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
choiceFeedback: Divide by 12 and look for a remainder: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6.
Find how many complete feet fit, then how many inches left over.
hints: 30 inches is more than 2 feet (24 in) but less than 3 feet (36 in) — so the answer is 2 feet plus some leftover inches.
Divide by 12 to find whole feet; the REMAINDER stays as inches.
Compute 30 ÷ 12: it goes in 2 whole times using up 24 inches. Subtract 30 − 24 to find the leftover inches.

onLevel.title: onLevel — Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Convert 80 ounces of bolts to pounds

onLevel.correctWork: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so you divide (not multiply): 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds. Changing to a bigger unit gives a smaller number.
hints: You are going from a smaller unit (ounces) to a larger unit (pounds). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a larger unit means fewer of them, so divide: 80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds.

onLevel.title: Find the Conversion Error
onLevel.correctWork: Since 3 feet = 1 yard, you divide by 3 (not multiply). 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yards.
hints: You're going from a smaller unit (feet) to a larger unit (yards). Should you multiply or divide?
Converting to a larger unit gives a smaller number. 6 feet ÷ 3 = 2 yards.

onLevel.prompt: A recipe says you need 5 feet of ribbon, but the store only sells ribbon in inches. Another recipe says you need 2 yards of fabric, but your ruler measures in feet. Convert both measurements and explain the steps you used. Which conversion factor did you use each time?
onLevel.sentenceFrame: 5 feet = ___ inches because ___. 2 yards = ___ feet because ___. The conversion factors I used were ___.
onLevel.hint: First convert 5 feet to inches, then compare that total to the store's ribbon-selling unit.
hints: There are two separate conversions: 5 feet → inches, and 2 yards → feet. Each uses a different conversion factor.
Both go from a bigger unit to a smaller unit, so both are multiplication. Name the factor you use each time.
Start the ribbon: 5 × 12, since every foot holds 12 inches. Then the fabric: 2 × 3, since every yard holds 3 feet.

extending.stem: Leg 1: The joystick rod is 3 feet long, but the parts catalog lists it in inches. How many inches is that? (1 ft = 12 in)
extending.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36 inches.

extending.stem: Leg 2: A power cable on the cabinet plan measures 2.5 kilometers across the whole arcade network. How many meters is that? (1 km = 1,000 m)
extending.explanation: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiply: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 meters.

extending.stem: Leg 3: The coin box weighs 5 pounds, but the shipping label needs the weight in ounces. How many ounces is that? (1 lb = 16 oz)
extending.explanation: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so multiply: 5 × 16 = 80 ounces.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Multiply or Divide?

workedExample.label: Convert 4 feet of side panel to inches

extending.correctWork: Inches are smaller than feet, so you multiply (not divide): 4 × 12 = 48 inches. The answer should be larger, not smaller, when changing to a smaller unit.
hints: You are going from a larger unit (feet) to a smaller unit (inches). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a smaller unit means more of them, so multiply: 4 × 12 = 48 inches.

extending.stem: Final Leg: The finished cabinet ships in a crate holding 8 quarts of packing gel, but the supplier sells gel by the gallon. How many gallons is that? (4 qt = 1 gal)
extending.explanation: Gallons are bigger than quarts, so divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 gallons.

extending.stem: How many inches are in 7 feet?
choiceFeedback: There are 12 inches in every foot.
hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.
Set up 7 × 12 — seven groups of 12 inches.

extending.stem: How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: There are 3 feet in every yard.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.
Set up 3 × 3 — three yards, each worth 3 feet.

extending.stem: How many ounces are in 4 pounds?
choiceFeedback: There are 16 ounces in every pound.
hints: The key fact: 1 pound = 16 ounces. You have 4 pounds and want ounces.
Pounds are bigger than ounces, so converting to ounces means multiplying by 16.
Set up 4 × 16. (Break it up: 4 × 10 = 40 and 4 × 6 = 24, then add.)

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — Which is the correct conversion of 5 yards to inches?
exitTicket.explanation: 5 yards × 3 = 15 feet. 15 feet × 12 = 180 inches. Or: 5 × 36 = 180 inches.
choiceFeedback: Convert 5 yards to feet, then feet to inches.
Start with: 5 yards = ? feet. Then convert to inches.
Remember: 1 yard = 3 feet, and 1 foot = 12 inches.
hints: Yards to inches is a TWO-step trip: yards → feet → inches (or use 1 yard = 36 inches in one jump).
Multiply twice: yards × 3 gives feet, then feet × 12 gives inches. Or multiply yards × 36 directly.
Step 1: 5 × 3 = 15 feet. Step 2: multiply that 15 by 12 to land on inches.
